IACV main object IMAGE ANALYSIS: - extract image features (edges, corners, regions) - match features among different images - track features along an image sequence (video) COMPUTER VISION: compute a model of the observed scene - 2D shape reconstruction - 3D shape reconstruction - Object recognition - Object localization - Action recognition

HOMEWORK • HOMEWORK on Theory: - A LONG AND DIFFICULT EXERCISE - INDIVIDUAL (no collaboration) - MANDATORY IN THE STANDARD EXAM - PUBLISHED in NOVEMBER - UNIQUE DEADLINE: within the 1° EXAM CALL (about end of January) - but still VALID IN FUTURE CALLS AND FUTURE YEARS - DEVELOPED IN MATLAB - EVALUATION based on (i) SUBMISSION and (ii) REPORT - FOLLOW DELIVERY INSTRUCTION: PUBLISHED at the same time as HOMEWORK

# Page 38^page=38
PROJECT • application PROJECT: - TEAMS of 1, 2, or 3 STUDENTS (collaboration is welcome) - MANDATORY IN STANDARD EXAM - LIST OF TOPICS: PUBLISHED MID DECEMBER, - DEVELOPED IN (ALMOST) ANY PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE - MANY DEADLINES = THREE DAYS BEFORE EACH EXAM CALL - EVALUATION based on - (i) SUBMITTED MATERIAL - (ii) pdf REPORT and ppt PRESENTATION - (iii) PRESENTATION/DISCUSSION - FOLLOW DELIVERY INSTRUCTIONS: published at the same time as TOPICS

# Page 39^page=39
Project evaluation: maximum score (20/30) is NOT the DEFAULT outcome. Here are some minimal requirements: • Awerness of the theory taught in the course: avoid unnecessary assumption or restrictions • Awereness of the theory taught in the course: avoid to re-invent (often worst) solutions • Awereness of the theory taught in the course: capability to autonomously apply theory to derive solutions • Autonomy in the retrieval and/or construction of the needed data sets • Experimental results based on real images, not only simulated ones • Development of a solution with a certain degree of generality, without tailoring it to just a single case (e.g., single video or image)

# Page 40^page=40
